The front (−z) is the river front on the Seine.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. river-front three-quarter of the whole long station-museum with arched vaults, central clock pavilion and pitched roof, daylight
  2. elevated view of the west end and entrance forecourt with its glass canopy and the vaulted roof behind
  3. street-side three-quarter at the pavilion end with the arched fronts and the barrel roof, dusk-light daylight

json.notes: A long former railway station now a museum: a stone Beaux-Arts river front of arcaded and arched storeys with a tall central clock pavilion, flanked by mansard-roofed hotel blocks at the west and an arched pavilion at the east end. Behind the facade, a barrel-vaulted glass hall rises above the stone, which is the signature feature. Stone is cream-coloured, the vault is grey-green glass and metal.
